proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true lag varies within-season or is shorter/longer than 2 weeks, forecasts may show phase shift (peak timing error) despite reasonable amplitude.
proposals.rationale: Anchor specification matching prior best: SEIRS captures waning immunity/reinfection dynamics; delayed_I with 2-week lag aligns with hospitalization reporting/admission lag and has shown better rolling robustness than shorter delays.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May reintroduce rolling instability/overreaction to week-to-week changes (timing jitter), especially around the peak, if the effective lag is closer to 2 weeks.
proposals.rationale: Near-neighborhood lag variant to test slightly faster hospitalization response while keeping the same parsimonious SEIRS backbone; may improve peak timing if admissions track infections more tightly in this age group.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Can oversmooth and lag the peak too much, underestimating rapid rises and producing late peak forecasts if the true lag is closer to 1–2 weeks.
proposals.rationale: Alternative nearby lag to accommodate slower admission/reporting dynamics and smoother high-scale series; can reduce sensitivity to short-term fluctuations by enforcing a longer effective delay.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May remain sensitive/overflexible across rolling splits (parameter non-identifiability in short series), yielding variable peak width/tail behavior and inconsistent multi-week forecasts.
proposals.rationale: Single fractional variant kept close to the anchor (same structure and delay) to potentially improve rolling stability via memory effects without changing observation semantics; included as a cautious robustness probe rather than a complexity jump in compartments.
